text: Water management (ការគ្រប់គ្រងទឹក) should begin with knowing whether a field is rain-fed (ពឹងទឹកភ្លៀង) or has dependable irrigation (ប្រព័ន្ធស្រោចស្រព). During the wet season (រដូវវស្សា, roughly May-October), the priority for many smallholders is managing excess rainfall and maintaining drainage, not just supplying more water. During the dry season (រដូវប្រាំង), water becomes a much stronger constraint, so farmers without reliable irrigation should be cautious about planting water-demanding crops, especially vegetables, where short water stress reduces quality but waterlogging damages roots. For rice, continuous flooding is not always necessary -- the right regime depends on the production system, field level, soil, and water availability. For cassava and established cashew, the goal is generally steady soil moisture without prolonged waterlogging; young plants need more attention than mature ones. Do not assume a Preah Vihear smallholder can simply 'irrigate when needed' -- limited access to pumps, wells, canals, or fuel can make irrigation expensive or unavailable. Practical advice should prioritize water conservation (ការរក្សាទឹក) first: good planting timing, soil cover, weed control, useful crop-residue retention, and drainage maintenance -- before recommending new irrigation infrastructure. Do not give a fixed irrigation frequency or water volume without knowing the crop, soil, growth stage, water source, and current weather. The practical hierarchy: (1) choose planting timing for expected rainfall, (2) know if the field is rain-fed or irrigated, (3) protect existing soil moisture, (4) maintain drainage during heavy rain, (5) prioritize water at the growth stages where stress causes the most yield loss, (6) use irrigation efficiently only where it's actually available.
